page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 resource ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations fall within the average range. While cached small-block memory read bandwidth is average at 565.97 GB/sec, uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths are weak, measuring 37.36 GB/sec and 14.86 GB/sec respectively. LLM inference capabilities are average for small 135M models but drop to weak or poor performance levels when executing medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-standard-8 offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for mainstream workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory or compute-optimized instances. Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density, this instance is well-suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database operations.
